title: Frontend: Detect data type in JS
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Detect data type in JS. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(entries). Entries are descriptor strings: null,array,date,map,set,nan,number,string,boolean,function,object. Construct each corresponding value and return diagnostic labels; null, arrays, NaN and supported built-ins need explicit handling before typeof.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Use explicit checks for null and Array.isArray before typeof-based primitive handling.
alternativeApproaches: Separate semantic validation of a value from a convenience diagnostic type label.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: null; array; NaN.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
